sources: asan types of sentences, transformation of sentences.pdf pp.1–8 (primary)

rules.rule_en: There are four types of sentences based on function: Assertive or Declarative, Interrogative, Imperative, and Exclamatory.
Assertive/Declarative sentences make a statement or assertion and end with a full stop.
Interrogative sentences are used to ask questions, interrogate, or make inquiries and end with a question mark.
Imperative sentences express a request, command, or instruction, usually ending with a period but occasionally an exclamation point.
Exclamatory sentences express strong feelings like surprise, wonder, or emotion and end with an exclamation mark.
Identify sentence types: Statement (Declarative), Interrogative, Imperative (Command/Request), and Exclamatory.
Transforming an assertive sentence into an imperative sentence involves restructuring the sentence to give a command, request, advice, or instruction.
General Rule: Remove the subject 'you' and begin with the verb. If the assertive sentence has 'should' or 'ought to', drop them and use the main verb directly.
If the assertive sentence expresses a duty or necessity, remove 'must' and begin directly with the verb.
If the assertive sentence contains 'never', keep 'never' at the beginning and remove 'should'.
If the assertive sentence contains 'It is necessary to', remove 'It is necessary to' and begin with the verb.
If the assertive sentence has 'Let us', it can be rewritten as 'Let's' for a suggestion.
If the subject is anything but except 'You', write 'Let' + objective form of that subject.
If the sentence is negative interrogative, change it to affirmative. If it is bare interrogative, change it to negative.
If there is no auxiliary verb in the sentence, change it by using do / does / did or don't / doesn't / didn't.
'Ever' in the interrogative sentence is replaced by 'never' in assertive sentences.
'Who' + 'don't/doesn't/didn't' in interrogative sentences is replaced by someone/somebody/everybody/everyone/no one/nobody/anybody/anyone in assertive sentences.
'Though/does it matter' is replaced by 'it doesn't matter'.
'Anything' in interrogative sentences is replaced by 'nothing' in assertive sentences.
Use 'not' before opposite words to change Assertive to Negative.
If the sentence of Comparative degree is Assertive then use 'not' in positive degree to make negative sentence.
If the sentence of positive degree is Affirmative then use 'not' in comparative degree to make negative sentence.
Replace 'alone' or 'only' with 'None but' at the start of the sentence.
'Always' in assertive changes to 'never fails to be, does not fail to' in negative.
Remove words like very, extremely and add 'what', 'how'. Remove (.) and add (!) in exclamatory sentence.
Add words like very, extremely, certainly; Remove (!) and add (.) in Assertive sentences. Exclamatory: What a surprise to see you here. Statement: It is indeed a surprise to see you here.
Use 'Will you' or 'Would you' for Politeness (Requests & Commands)
Use 'Can you' or 'Could you' for Asking Ability-based Requests
Use 'Shall I / Shall we' for Suggestions
Use 'Why don't you' for Advice or Suggestions
Use 'Do you mind' for Polite Requests
Use 'Is it possible to' for Formal Requests
Use 'Would you mind' for Extra Politeness
Use 'It is good/nice/great that...' to express admiration or approval
Use 'You are so kind/generous/wonderful to...' to express admiration or approval
Use 'I appreciate your...' to express admiration or approval
Use 'It is admirable that...' to express admiration or approval
Use 'Well done for...' to express admiration or approval
To change an imperative sentence to passive voice, use 'You are requested to' (for polite requests) or 'You are warned/ordered to' (for warnings/commands).
To change a request from Active to Passive voice, replace 'Please' with 'You are requested to'. If the request is negative, use 'You are requested not to'.

7. Stop hitting me.

I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 2. She wants to go out.
I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 3. We do not hate the poor.
I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 4. We should have the courage to say the right things.
worked_exercises.answer_en: Have the courage to say the right things.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 5. We should take care of our health.

I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 9. Would you post the letter for me, please?
worked_exercises.answer_en: Please post the letter for me.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 10. Who does not like to be praised?
worked_exercises.answer_en: Let everyone like to be praised.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 11. You should do the work.
I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 12. He should do the work.
I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 13. You should always tell the truth.
I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 14. You are asked to help me.
I. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 1: 15. We should not break the rules of the college.
worked_exercises.answer_en: Do not break the rules of the college.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: II. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 2: 1. You should complete your homework.
II. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 2: 2. We must respect our elders.
II. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 2: 3. He should wait outside.
II. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 2: 4. You must not waste your time.
II. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 2: 5. It is necessary to follow the instructions.
II. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 2: 6. You must obey traffic rules.

II. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 2: 9. You ought to be kind to others.
II. Interchange Statement to Imperatives - 2: 10. It is important to keep your surroundings clean.
III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 1. What though we happen to be late?
worked_exercises.answer_en: It does not matter though we happen to be late.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 2. Why waste time in reading trash?
worked_exercises.answer_en: It is useless to waste time in reading trash.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 3. Were we sent into the world simply to make money?
worked_exercises.answer_en: We were not sent into the world simply to make money.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 4. How can man die better than facing fearful odds?
worked_exercises.answer_en: Man cannot die better than facing fearful odds.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 5. When can their glory fade?
III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 6. Was he not a villain to do such a deed?
worked_exercises.answer_en: He was indeed a villain to do such a deed.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 7. Who can touch pitch without being defiled?
worked_exercises.answer_en: No one can touch pitch without being defiled.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 8. Can any man by taking thought add a cubit to his stature?
worked_exercises.answer_en: No man can by taking thought add a cubit to his stature.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 9. What though the field be lost?
worked_exercises.answer_en: It does not matter though the field be lost.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 10. Is that the way a gentleman should behave?
worked_exercises.answer_en: That is not the way a gentleman should behave.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 11. Who does not know the owl?
III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 12. Shall I ever forget those happy days?
worked_exercises.answer_en: I shall never forget those happy days.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: III. Interchange Interrogative to Statements - 1: 13. Who is so wicked as to amuse himself with the infirmities of extreme old age?
worked_exercises.answer_en: No one is so wicked as to amuse himself with the infirmities of extreme old age.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: 3. Alas that youth should pass away!

worked_exercises.prompt_en: 2. Turn off the lights.
